questions.questionText:
An economy with few resources is encouraged to improve the quality of its human resources.
Which policy will lead to such an improvement?

options.text: conserving and protecting more of its natural resources
limiting the immigration of skilled labour
providing more opportunities for education and training
reducing the use of machines in production

questions.questionText:
A country raises the school leaving age from 15 to 17 years.
What is the opportunity cost of this increased period of school education to the young people
affected?

options.text: costs of training and employing more teachers
financial help necessary for school leavers who go to university
government expenditure on building extra classrooms
lost income from paid employment because of school attendance

questions.questionText:
In a market there is a shortage of a good.
What change would cause the market to come to an equilibrium?

options.text: a decrease in supply
a fall in price
an increase in demand
a rise in price

questions.questionText:
A product has a totally inelastic price elasticity of demand.
What will happen to total revenue if the price of the product falls by 25%?

options.text: It will fall by 25%.
It will fall to zero.
It will remain unchanged.
It will rise by 25%.

questions.questionText:
In 2014, a plan for a major new rail link funded by central and regional government was
announced. It would involve the redevelopment of a city area, generate 14000 jobs and allow the
development of 2000 homes and offices for private businesses.
What economic concepts are indicated directly in the above statement?

options.text: budget surplus and inflation
factors of production and multinational companies
fiscal policy and mixed economy
regional unemployment and average wage rates

questions.questionText: How are social costs calculated?

options.text: fixed costs plus variable costs
private benefits less private costs
private costs plus external costs
social benefits less external costs

questions.questionText:
What is a disadvantage for a trade union representing workers in a company that has increased
specialisation?

options.text: Capital equipment can be substituted for labour.
Different abilities can be used fully.
Production levels are decreased.
Workers are able to gain a higher level of skill.

questions.questionText:
A government finance minister said that the purchasing power of most people’s incomes had
risen in the last year.
What must have increased for the purchasing power to rise?

options.text: money wages
net income after tax
real wages
wage rates

options.text: All occupations were better off in 2013 than in 2003.

Non-manual workers had lower percentage increases in income than manual workers.

doctor window cleaner

Both workers save 10% of their disposable income.
How much is this in each case?
doctor window cleaner
What is most likely to increase a firm’s profits?

options.text: government controls on its prices
grants for the purchase of new machines
an increase in the wages paid to its workers
rising costs of its raw materials

questions.questionText:
Sohrab bought shares in a French telecommunications company operating in many countries.
Joel owns and runs a mobile telephone accessories and repair shop.
What is not identified above?

options.text: multinational company
partnership
public company
sole proprietor

What is the firm’s total revenue and the price of the product?
total revenue price

Which firm has the highest average cost of production?
fixed costs variable costs

Other things being equal, what is likely to decrease public spending?

options.text: an increase in the age of retirement
an increase in the birth rate
an increase in the school-leaving age
an increase in unemployment

questions.questionText: When is a tax regressive?

options.text: when some goods have a lower tax than others
when the tax as a proportion of income decreases as income increases
when the tax is linked to the rate of inflation
when the tax is on incomes rather than on goods or services

questions.questionText:
The Government of India wishes to help the very poorest people.
Which policy would be most likely to achieve this?

options.text: lowering capital gains tax
lowering housing subsidies
lowering indirect taxation
lowering inheritance tax

questions.questionText:
Suppose the Indian Government raises the rate of interest.
What is likely to be the direct effect on the economy?

options.text: It will raise any deficit on the current account.
It will raise the economic growth rate.
It will raise the foreign exchange rate.
It will raise the inflation rate.

questions.questionText: What is involved in the construction of a retail price index?

options.text: a basket of goods
average incomes
economic growth rate
income tax rate

questions.questionText: What identifies a recession?

options.text: a fall in the general price level
a fall in the level of national output
a fall in the real value of money
a fall in the stock market index

questions.questionText:
The table shows the percentage changes in earnings and consumer prices for four countries for
one year.
Which country is likely to have experienced the greatest increase in real income during the year?
country earnings consumer prices

options.text: France +6.5 +3.5
Germany +4.0 +4.0

questions.questionText:
In the US Consumer Price Index (CPI), food has a weighting of 13.7%. In India food has a
weighting of 46.2% in the CPI.
What can be concluded from this?

options.text: Consumers in India spend more on food than US consumers.
Food is a bigger proportion of consumer spending in India than in the US.
The farming sector’s output of food is higher in India than in the US.
The price of food is rising more rapidly in India than in the US.

questions.questionText:
In many developing economies there is a high rate of population growth.
What is a cause of this?

options.text: Jobseekers migrate from rural to urban centres.
Poor people have many children to provide labour on family farms.
There is increased resistance to life saving drugs.
There is not enough clean water.

questions.questionText:
A country has a birth rate of 30 per 1000 and a death rate of 35 per 1000 and no migration.
What is most likely to cause the population to fall?

options.text: The birth rate decreases and the death rate increases.
The birth rate increases and the death rate remains the same.
The birth rate remains constant and the death rate decreases.
The increase in the birth rate is greater than the increase in the death rate.

questions.questionText: What is likely to cause a rise in a country’s foreign exchange rate?

options.text: a fall in its exports of goods and services
a fall in its imports of goods and services
a fall in its inflow of income
a rise in its outflow of transfers

questions.questionText:
Drinks producers in India are resisting plans to remove tariffs on imported drinks. They claim that
a reduction in tariffs would destroy the emerging drinks industry with large-scale imports of cheap
drinks.
Which argument for protectionism are they putting forward?

options.text: the declining industry argument
the infant industry argument
the strategic industry argument
the sunset industry argument

questions.questionText: Who is most likely to benefit if India bans all steel imports?

options.text: buyers of steel in India
foreign steel producers
Indian firms buying steel
Indian firms selling steel at home

questions.questionText: What is certain to encourage a higher level of international trade?

options.text: conservation of resources and unstable exchange rates
exploitation of resources and wider use of quotas
increased support for home industries and increased tariffs
